tagline: Forty-three US cities, four crime categories, FBI figures projected to 2025, ranked by rate rather than raw counts, in one HTML file you can email to somebody.
launchSub: Satellite map · rankings · city detail · search, sort and filter
titleTail: 43 cities in a single HTML file
lede: Counting incidents ranks cities by population and tells you nothing. Everything in Per Capita is per 100,000 residents, with the year-over-year change beside it, so a bad year reads differently from a bad decade. It was built for someone who wanted to look at the numbers himself instead of reading someone's summary of them, and grew from 15 cities to 43.

features.d: colour-coded markers sized by population on a satellite map, following whichever category you pick.
FBI rates 40%, dispatch density 20%, NeighborhoodScout 15%, CAP Index 15%, OpenCrime and SafeWise 10%. Modeled figures are labelled as modeled.
search, sort any column, filter by size or state, open a city for its detail against national averages.
one file: double-click it from a USB stick, an email or a desktop folder. Only the map tiles need a connection.

cards.html: Voluntary reporting: a city that looks safe may simply have reported less. Definition drift: category boundaries shift between standards. City limits aren't metros. Small denominators: a handful of incidents swings a small city's rate, so rank order at the bottom is noise.
Leaflet for the map, FBI city figures baked in as a JSON literal, all state in memory. No fetch, no API key to expire, no build.

scope: Figures are projected to 2025 with the FBI's national trend, not measured. A dashboard that hides its seams makes people confident about things they shouldn't be.
closing: Look at the numbers yourself. Then look at the caveats.
